newsitem.title: FINLAND: Quiet Finnish bonds rise but lag Germany.
newsitem.headline: Quiet Finnish bonds rise but lag Germany.

text.p: Bonds were higher but trade quiet in the early afternoon on Tuesday after a rise in the morning as a fall in German M3 boosted Bunds, but the market lagged its German benchmarks, dealers said.
The long-end yield gap over Germany widended to 25 basis points. "That is typical when the market rises," one dealer said. "Once we catch up, we will go back towards 20 bps."

The markka was steady against the mark, taking cover from a fall in the Swedish crown in the morning and dealers said interest was scant. The near-term range was seen 2.98-3.00 per mark, but views were mixed on what a new dollar rally would do.
One senior forex dealer said the markka could ease against the German unit even if the dollar started rising again.

"That could prompt dollar buying for markka too ... and it is not evident that a dollar rally would boost all crosses against the mark," he said, but added that there was little in sight to boost the dollar much.

The U.S. policy setting Federal Open Market Committee meting was seen holding rates and the dollar's correction lower last week together with M3 in line with Bundesbank's target were seen taking pressure off the German central bank to up its repo rate.
